thread.title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Mixed as Trade Concerns Weigh on Markets; Tech Sector Continues Rebound

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Mixed as Trade Concerns Weigh on Markets; Tech Sector Continues Rebound
text:
Shutterstock photo Major US stock indices were mixed around midday on Wednesday amid fresh trade dispute concerns and with tech heavy Nasdaq in green territory following a robust earnings report from device maker Apple ( AAPL ).
In economic news, Automated Data Processing reported private payrolls increased 219,000 in July, beating the 173,000 expected.
The final July Markit manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index eased to 55.3 (55.5 preliminary and consensus) after falling 1.0 point to 55.4 in June.
The Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing index dropped 2.1 points to 58.1 in July, below the 59.5 expected, after a 1.5 point increase to 60.2 in June.
Construction spending posted a surprise decline of 1.1% in June vs estimates for a 0.3% gain, while May's previously 0.4% gain was revised sharply higher to 1.3%.
In Europe, equities largely fell as the trade spat between the US and China returned to the center stage following a report that some White House advisers are urging President Donald Trump to hike planned tarriffs on $200 billion in Chinese imports to 25% versus the 10% originally proposed.
Crude oil is down 1.77% to $67.54 per barrel. Natural gas is down 0.58% to $2.766 per 1 million BTU. Gold is down 0.46% to $1,227.90 an ounce, while silver is down 0.73% to $15.445 an ounce. Copper is down 2.63% to $2.757 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund is down 1.61% to $14.05, with the United States Natural Gas Fund is down 0.22% to $22.76. Amongst precious-metal funds, the VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF is down 0.40% to $21.20, while SPDR Gold Shares is down 0.48% to $115.43. The iShares Silver Trust is down 0.73% to $14.50.
